response.passage: In the small village of Pochampally, the Sahyog Weaving Cooperative has changed how local artisans work. Before 2015, weavers sold their fabrics to middlemen for very low prices. To solve this, a local leader named Ravi Kumar organized 45 families to form the cooperative. By pooling their resources, the weavers could buy high-quality silk directly from suppliers in Bangalore. This change happened because the cooperative allowed them to bypass the middlemen, ensuring the weavers kept the full profit. Today, the cooperative produces 120 sarees every month. However, the work is difficult. Because the looms require constant physical effort, many weavers feel exhausted by the evening. Some outsiders mistakenly think the weavers are 'tired' of their profession, but they actually love their craft. The cooperative has brought prosperity, proving that collective action is more effective than working alone. Ravi Kumar often says that the success of the group depends on the dedication of every single member. The village has become a model for others, showing that when people unite, they can control their own economic future.
response.summary: The Sahyog Weaving Cooperative in Pochampally helps local weavers earn better profits by selling directly to suppliers. By working together, the families have improved their economic situation despite the physically demanding nature of the work.
